title: NFC Review Card vs QR Review Stand — Choosing the Right Google Review Prompt
summary: Local businesses choose between NFC review cards and QR review stands based on customer engagement moment, staff capability, venue layout and desired conversion rates. NFC review cards deliver premium tactile experience and fast interaction at high-value checkout moments where staff actively prompt guests to leave feedback with 20-30% success rates when staff engagement is consistent and systematic. Cards use NTAG213 passive tags embedded in quality cardstock with custom branding, cost $0.50-2.00 per unit at volume, and require active staff prompting to achieve meaningful conversion. The tap interaction completes in 1-2 seconds at the moment of highest engagement. QR review stands work better as persistent visual static prompts on tabletops, windows, entrance areas, and menu inserts where spontaneous discovery drives engagement without requiring any staff intervention, though with lower 5-15% conversion rates reflecting delayed timing. QR stands cost $5-15 per unit depending on material and finish and work with 100% of smartphones equipped with cameras. Cost-per-completed-review analysis shows NFC at $2.50-10 per review when staff actively engage, versus QR at $50-150 per review. This comparison helps restaurants, salons, spas, fitness centers, and service businesses evaluate which format aligns with actual customer journey, staff training capacity, venue layout and operational complexity. ProudTek recommends testing both formats with 50-100 samples each over 3-4 weeks to measure real conversion impact and customer behavior before scaling to production.

sections.title: When to Choose NFC Review Cards
sections.intro: NFC cards work best when staff can actively introduce the card at a natural handoff moment.

before: Expecting customers to scan QR without staff introduction or visual cue
Trying to place NFC cards where phones remain in pockets during checkout
Staff already overloaded and cannot add review-card prompting to their workflow
after: Server hands card to guest at payment or service completion moment
Counter staff can train to offer card as part of closure checklist
Smartphone on table or in guest's hand where NFC tap feels natural
Premium feeling card reinforces brand and creates memorable review prompt

sections.title: When to Choose QR Review Stands
sections.intro: QR codes work best as persistent visual prompts that operate independently of staff intervention.
bullets: Tabletop placement — customers eat while waiting for check and naturally notice a small standing QR card
Window or entrance display — QR codes for Google reviews on business windows reach customers before they enter, collecting feedback on the way out
Menu inserts — QR codes printed on menus or table tents are discovered during the meal experience without staff effort
Self-service venues — coffee shops, fast-casual and food trucks where staff interaction is minimal rely on visual QR placement
High-volume environments — restaurants with 100+ covers per service cannot reliably hand out NFC cards to every guest

sections.title: Implementation Framework
sections.intro: Use this workflow to test both formats and determine which drives better review volume for your venue.

items.label: Week 1 — Prepare samples
items.text: Order 50-100 NFC cards with your Google review link and 3-5 QR stands with matching redirect. Test both on your team before customer exposure.

items.label: Week 2-3 — NFC card pilot
items.text: Brief your staff on NFC prompt moment and actively offer cards to every guest during service. Track which staff members prompt consistently and which need reinforcement.

items.label: Week 4 — QR stand pilot
items.text: Place QR stands on 3-4 tables in high-visibility positions. Use different table locations to identify the spot with highest scan rates.

items.label: Week 5-6 — Measure results
items.text: Track review volume and timestamp data from both formats. Measure staff adoption rate for NFC prompting and customer notice rate for QR placement.

items.label: Week 7 — Decide and scale
items.text: Choose the winner or adopt hybrid model (NFC at checkout, QR on tables). Scale successful format and discontinue or archive the underperformer.

sections.title: Technical Setup and Reliability
sections.intro: Both formats require proper link configuration and fallback handling to maximize review conversion.

features.title: NFC link targeting
features.text: NFC card must point to mobile-optimized Google review link. Ensure link opens Google Business Profile directly, not your homepage.

features.title: QR link redirect
features.text: QR code should use redirect service (bit.ly, your domain) to track scan volume and allow link updates without reprinting.

features.title: Conversion timing
features.text: NFC reviews happen 30-60 seconds after tap while guest is engaged. QR reviews happen later, often on the way out or next day.

features.title: Verification testing
features.text: Test both NFC and QR formats on different phone models before production. Confirm Android and iOS compatibility.

features.title: Analytics tracking
features.text: Use Google Business Profile insights or UTM parameters to measure which format drives higher review volume and quality.

features.title: Fallback handling
features.text: Include handwritten business name and Google search phrase as backup for customers whose phones have issues with NFC or QR.

sections.title: Cost-Per-Review Analysis
sections.intro: The true value of each format emerges when you calculate cost per completed review, not just cost per card or stand.

dataHighlight.heading: Lower cost-per-review for NFC when staff actively prompt
dataHighlight.text: When staff actively offer NFC cards at checkout, the cost per completed review (accounting for card cost and success rate) is 3-5x lower than QR stands. However, this advantage evaporates if staff prompting drops below 80% consistency. QR stands require no staff behavior change and maintain steady performance without management overhead.

faq.question: Will all smartphones work with NFC review cards?
faq.answer: No. NFC works on approximately 95% of modern Android phones and 100% of iPhone 11 and newer models. Older iPhones (iPhone XS and earlier, except iPhone XR) cannot read NFC. You should offer QR as a fallback for non-NFC phones. Most businesses find that the 5% incompatibility rate is acceptable given NFC's superior user experience.

faq.question: How much should I invest in NFC card stock versus QR stands?
faq.answer: Test both formats with minimal upfront investment: order 100 NFC cards ($50-200) and 5 QR stands ($25-75). Run a 3-4 week pilot where staff actively promote NFC cards while QR stands sit on tables. Measure review volume from both formats, then scale the winner. Most venues find one format dominates by 2-3x after the pilot.

faq.question: Should I include a QR fallback on my NFC card?
faq.answer: Yes. Include a small QR code on the back or corner of your NFC card so customers whose phones lack NFC capability can still leave reviews. This removes the excuse of technical incompatibility and captures the ~5% of guests with older iPhones or non-NFC Android devices.

faq.question: How do I measure which format is driving more reviews?
faq.answer: Use Google Business Profile insights to see when reviews are submitted. NFC reviews arrive 30-60 seconds after the customer-facing moment (at the table or checkout counter). QR reviews arrive later, often 5-30 minutes or the next day. You can also use short URLs (bit.ly) for QR codes to track total clicks. For NFC, you can watermark the review moment by analyzing timestamp clusters.

faq.question: What if my staff forgets to offer the NFC card?
faq.answer: This is NFC's main weakness. If staff prompting drops below 70%, QR stands often outperform NFC by sheer visibility. To maximize NFC success, make it part of the closing checklist, train your team regularly, and tie the review goal to staff performance metrics. Some venues keep NFC cards visible on the counter so customers ask for them proactively.

faq.question: Can I use the same Google review link for both NFC and QR?
faq.answer: Yes. Both formats redirect to the same Google Business Profile review page. ProudTek recommends using a redirect URL (your domain or bit.ly) for the QR code so you can track scan volume separately from direct link traffic. Your NFC card can point directly to the review link or use the same redirect URL for unified analytics.

faq.question: How long do NFC cards stay usable before degrading?
faq.answer: NFC cards typically remain functional for 2-3 years of regular handling, though the cardstock may show wear. The NTAG213 chip inside is rated for 1 million read cycles, so the card will outlast most physical handling scenarios. QR stands on rigid material last indefinitely if protected from extreme weather.

faq.question: Should I customize the card or stand design with my branding?
faq.answer: Yes. Custom branding increases perceived value of NFC cards and reinforces brand presence during the review moment. For QR stands, custom design helps the code feel intentional rather than generic. The design investment (artwork, setup fee) typically costs $100-300 per format and is worth it if you're ordering 1000+ units. For smaller pilots, keep design simple.
